newsitem.title: CHINA: Social stability prime concern of Chinese - poll.
newsitem.headline: Social stability prime concern of Chinese - poll.

text.p: China's social stability is the major concern of the majority of its population, but the number of people who think so is falling, according to a recent poll, the Business News said on Thursday.

In a survey of 1,020 families in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong and Wuhan at the end of last year, 47.9 percent of those polled rated social stability as a top priority, down from 52 percent at the end of 1995.
Social welfare came in as the second most important concern of the people polled, with 31.3 percent giving it top priority, the newspaper said.
Corruption of officials remained in third place.
Relations between China and Taiwan topped foreign policy concerns, the newspaper said. Beijing regards the island as a renegade province.
